title: Potential as a Readout: Witnessed Envelopes, Two-Layer Agency, and the Measurement of Pseudo-Peace
note: K0 epistemic note, version 2 (tier-raising pass). Has seven explicit numbered display equations (1)-(7) plus one unnumbered chain-rule identity, four proved lemmas L1-L4 (Sec.5), seven non-collapse distinctions D1-D7 stated as X≠Y (Sec.3), four falsifiable propositions P-A..P-D (Sec.8), and an exact numeric identifiability certificate (Sec.4.5). Labels below use the author's own numbering/lettering where the paper gives one (eq.(N), D1-D7, L1-L4, P-A..P-D); items without an author label are marked 'unnumbered'.

equations.section: Sec. 4.2, The joint event and the envelope
equations.text: p*_{A,g}(h,z;T,B,P) := max_{π∈Πwit_A(g;h,z,T,B)} Pr^π_P(Rg ∩ Dg ∩ Xg ∩ Fg), with p*_{A,g} := 0 when the set is empty
equations.meaning: Corrigible agency potential restated on the witnessed set: the maximum joint probability of reading, actor-directed deciding, causal enacting, and usable feedback, taken over the finite set of policies with an actual comparable-use record.

equations.section: Sec. 4.2, The joint event and the envelope
equations.meaning: The primary objects are a profile of potentials across tasks and a capability set of tasks clearing a declared threshold α.

equations.section: Sec. 4.2, The joint event and the envelope
equations.text: A^corr_A(h,z;T,B,P,w) := Σ_g w_g p*_{A,g} ∈ [0,1]
equations.meaning: A weighted scalar summary of the potential profile, valid only for comparing interventions under one declared weighting w.

equations.label: unnumbered
equations.section: Sec. 4.2, The joint event and the envelope
equations.text: p_{A,g}(π) = r·d·x·f, with r = Pr(Rg), d = Pr(Dg|Rg), x = Pr(Xg|Rg,Dg), f = Pr(Fg|Rg,Dg,Xg)
equations.meaning: Chain-rule factorization for one policy on one task; the maximum in (1) is taken of the product under one policy, never of the four factors separately.

equations.section: Sec. 4.3, Two layers
equations.text: p*(2)_{A,g} := max_{z∈Jfeas} p*_{A,g}(h,z;T,B,P)
equations.meaning: Layer-2 potential: the best achievable potential after also optimizing over feasible structural interventions z, as opposed to layer-1 potential at fixed z.

equations.section: Sec. 4.3, Two layers
equations.text: L^recoverable_A = max_{z∈Jfeas} A^corr_A(h,z) − A^corr_A(h,z0)
equations.meaning: The recoverable gap: the difference between the best achievable corrigible-agency envelope under feasible structural change and the envelope under present conditions z0; the part of Galtung's baseline gap a study can subtract with a record behind it.

equations.section: Sec. 4.4, Corrigibility and spectral support made readable
equations.text: Δspec(Ri) > 0 ⟺ channel_i = open ∧ Ṙ_i ≠ 0
equations.meaning: A readout-level sufficient condition for a subgroup retaining spectral support, built from two retained-record tests: an open correction channel and a nonzero repair rate.

equations.section: Sec. 6, Pseudo-peace: a gate collapse with a numerical signature
equations.text: Yobs = calm ∧ p*wit = low ∧ F = blocked
equations.meaning: Pseudo-peace defined as three readouts taken together: an evaluator reads calm, the witnessed potential is low, and the feedback/objection channel is blocked.

equations.label: PAR-stepper
equations.section: Sec. 5, Setting (forced Laplacian model)
equations.text: LR = DW − W (forced Laplacian); A := LR + Γ; s[n+1] = s[n] + dt(−A s[n] + J)
equations.meaning: The discrete linear spine the programme's core forces: a forced-Laplacian generator plus dissipation, driving a stepper equation under constant load J, on which the bounded-suppression lemmas are proved.

equations.label: L1
equations.section: Sec. 5, Lemmas (invariance and recurrence)
equations.text: s* = A^{-1}J is the unique fixed point independent of u; ∥s[n]−s*∥ ≤ ρ^{n−nB}∥s[nB]−s*∥ after the last nonzero tick of a bounded intervention; if s*_i > θ there is an explicit finite N* after which s_i[n] > θ for all n ≥ nB+N*
equations.meaning: A bounded amplitude-only intervention cannot move the fixed point; the state returns to threshold-crossing after a finite, computable number of ticks once the intervention ends — proved recurrence.

equations.label: L2
equations.section: Sec. 5, Lemmas (the bill)
equations.text: |u_i[n]| = dt[(γ_i+D_i)(s*_i−θ) − Σ_{k≠i} W_ik(s*_k−s_k[n])], converging to a rate F_i^∞ > 0 whenever s*_i ≥ θ, so cumulative force is F_i^∞·n + o(n)
equations.meaning: Holding the state at threshold from some point on requires a non-vanishing per-tick force whose cumulative cost grows at least linearly in time held — the amplitude-suppression 'bill'.

equations.label: L3
equations.section: Sec. 5, Lemmas (operator change)
equations.text: s*'_i = s*_i / (1+ΔB_ii) with B = A^{-1} (Sherman–Morrison); any θ < s*_i is reached below with Δ > Δ* = (s*_i/θ − 1)/B_ii, and zero ongoing force
equations.meaning: Unlike amplitude suppression, raising dissipation γ_i (an operator-level change) can push the fixed point permanently below threshold with zero ongoing force cost.

equations.label: L4
equations.section: Sec. 5, Lemmas (mutation)
equations.text: s_j ≳ (J_j + W_ij·s̄_i)/(γ_j+D_j), with s̄_i an explicit increasing function of node i's own inflow, under permanent periodic resets of node i
equations.meaning: Suppressing one node under permanent resets produces a strictly positive long-run floor in a coupled neighbour node, formalizing mutation/tunneling of instability to another channel.

equations.label: D1 (NC-78)
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Potential ≠ exercised ≠ observed
equations.meaning: The envelope p* of what an agent could do, the policy actually used, and the evaluator's instrument readout are three readouts of three different latents.

equations.label: D2
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Declared set ≠ witnessed set
equations.meaning: A feasible set someone writes down is a declaration; only the set of options with an actual comparable-use record is a readout, finite and enumerable in the required sense.

equations.label: D3
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Layer 1 ≠ layer 2
equations.meaning: Choosing within a constraint structure C is one capacity; changing C itself is another, carried as an open conjecture pending a named test (P-D).

equations.label: D4
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Task potential ≠ aggregate potential
equations.meaning: A profile over tasks p* = (p*_g)_g is the real object; a weighted scalar is only a summary that can hide compression in one task behind a rise in another.

equations.label: D5
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Feasible ≠ permitted
equations.meaning: What has a working path is not the same as what present power currently allows; the feasible set must never be defined by the permitting authority.

equations.label: D6 (NC-79)
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Diagnosis of compression ≠ attribution of responsibility
equations.meaning: That a capability set has shrunk is read from an obstruction ledger and cost asymmetry; who is responsible is answered only by a separate act naming a chooser.

equations.label: D7
equations.section: Sec. 3, An anatomy of 'potential': seven distinctions
equations.text: Recoverable gap ≠ accumulated loss
equations.meaning: A gap a feasible intervention within the study horizon can reopen is one quantity; damage already fixed into history is another; a recoverable gap of zero is not evidence that no violence occurred.

equations.label: P-A
equations.section: Sec. 8, Falsifiable propositions
equations.text: Pseudo-peace signature: amplitude-suppressing interventions raise the calm an evaluator reads while p*wit does not rise and F stays blocked. Defeated if p*wit rises consistently with observed calm under such interventions.
equations.meaning: First falsifiable proposition, tied to the pseudo-peace regime.

equations.label: P-B
equations.section: Sec. 8, Falsifiable propositions
equations.text: Channel shift: when F is blocked and C^α shrinks in task g, load rises in a coupled task g' while the aggregate (3) stays flat. Defeated if profiles stay flat across tasks.
equations.meaning: Second falsifiable proposition, on load displacement between tasks.

equations.label: P-C
equations.section: Sec. 8, Falsifiable propositions
equations.text: The excluded path: groups whose min_i |C^α_i| falls while the mean rises show persistent cost concentration (CE-30) and higher recurrence than groups whose minimum does not fall. Defeated if no difference is found.
equations.meaning: Third falsifiable proposition, on hidden cost concentration inside a rising mean.

equations.label: P-D
equations.section: Sec. 8, Falsifiable propositions
equations.text: Layer 2 dominates the structural case: in cases classified as structural, the gap closable by layer-2 interventions exceeds the gap closable by layer-1 ones. Defeated if information-only or within-C interventions close as much.
equations.meaning: Fourth falsifiable proposition, the named test for the D3 layer-1/layer-2 conjecture.

equations.label: PAR-cert
equations.section: Sec. 4.5, Identifiability (an exact certificate)
equations.text: P1: r=d=x=9/10, channel always open, every reason voiced ⇒ f_P1=1, p*_P1=729/1000. P2: channel open w.p. 1/5, every open-channel reason voiced ⇒ f_P2=1/5, p*_P2=729/5000. Both induce the identical record Pr(complaint)=1/10.
equations.meaning: An exact worked example showing two declared models can agree on every observable record yet imply a five-fold difference in true potential, so the record alone supports only the interval [729/5000, 729/1000].
